nodes.title: Removing the good-dihedral hypothesis
nodes.statement: Fix r≥0 and assume HypD r, imported from R27.2: every S-type good-dihedral residual representation of odd characteristic with 2^(r+1) not dividing its prime-to-characteristic conductor is modular. Then every S-type ρ̄ of any characteristic p with 2^(r+1) not dividing N(ρ̄) is modular, subject only to k(ρ̄)=2 when p=2 and r=0. For r≥1, both classical dyadic weights two and four are admitted. No good-dihedral hypothesis is imposed on the conclusion's input.
hypotheses: S-type means continuous, odd and absolutely irreducible of dimension two over a finite field. N is the positive prime-to-p Artin conductor, retaining wild exponents.

For odd p normalize the weight by the R15.4 cyclotomic twisting recipe, which does not assume modularity. This preserves the prime-to-p conductor and projective image. After proving the normalized twist modular, use odd coefficient-prime stripping, the tame-level theta theorem and the controlled Katz-to-classical modularity comparison to untwist; this qualitative comparison may shift weight and does not need the same-weight lifting input of gap G1. Handle cyclotomic-reducible image by induction from a character and solvable residual modularity. At p=2 handle solvable image by R17.6 qualitative residual modularity.

Theorem5.1(2) at the original characteristic, Theorem5.1(4) at p′, and two applications of the exact odd-prime KW I Theorem4.1 export are the lifting inputs. Hypothesis(H), Theorem9.1 and the final modularity characterization of all compatible systems are not inputs.
proofSteps: Build the first type-(2) system C and use auxiliary-characteristic-choice to terminate in modularity or choose p′. Apply the prime-field Lemma 8.2 to C̄_p′; remove finitely many primes to choose q>p′. Its local shape and p′|q+1 meet R24.3/theorem-5-1-part-4-level-two-type-at-q; combine that lift with R24.5/kw-theorem-5-1-systems to obtain C′ linked to C at p′. Use these direct suppliers rather than the redundant R27.1 insertion node, whose extra all-ramified-primes bound must instead refer to prime-to-p′ support.

Track the dyadic exponent A=a(WD_2(C)). If p is odd, minimality at 2 gives A=v₂(N(ρ̄))≤r. If p=2 and k=2, its inertial WD parameter is (1⊕1,0), so A=0. If p=2 and k=4, it is (id,N_mon≠0), so A=2−dim ker N_mon=1; the theorem’s weight restriction excludes r=0 in that case.

Put b=v₂(N(C̄_p′)) and A′=a(WD_2(C′)). Reduction gives b≤A. Minimality of the second lift at 2 gives A′=b, since 2 differs from p′ and q. Let s be the largest prime below p′; reduction gives v₂(N(C̄′_s))≤A′=b≤A≤r. These are bounds; residual conductor can drop.

Let s be the largest prime below p′, so s>2. The two distinct nontrivial p′-power inertia characters at q survive modulo s and Frobenius interchanges their eigenspaces; hence the local, and therefore global, residual representation is absolutely irreducible. Oddness and continuity come from C′. The common WD conductor of C′ has support outside q below p′: p′ is crystalline of weight two, although the residual p′-representation itself can ramify at p′. A characteristic-s member may additionally ramify at s. Lemma 8.2 supplies all congruences at primes ≤p′−1, so C̄′_s is good-dihedral with t=p′>max(5,s,Q(N(C̄′_s)/q²)). The image theorem gives nonsolvability.

HypD r makes C̄′_s modular. Nonsolvability gives cyclotomic absolute irreducibility. Apply the exact odd-prime KW Theorem 4.1 export: C′_s is odd, finitely ramified and potentially semistable of weight two (crystalline weight two if s is outside the common support). Transfer its modularity to C′ through good Frobenius polynomials. At the shared nonsolvable residual representation in characteristic p′, C_p′ is crystalline of weight two, with cyclotomic absolute irreducibility; apply the same export and transfer through C back to the original residual member. Untwist as specified above when the initial normalization was nontrivial.
acceptance: At p=2,k=4,r=1 the original N is odd but A=1. This case passes HypD 1 after switching; it cannot be justified using HypD 0.
At p=2,k=2,r=0, A=0 and both reductions keep dyadic exponent zero.
For r=2 an exponent-two conductor is allowed; for r=1 it is forbidden. Replacing conductor by its radical would fail this check.
Use 0≤b≤A rather than equality at reduction, and use the intermediate C̄_p′, not the original ρ̄, to define the second minimal lift.
The condition on support is a condition on the prime-to-coefficient conductor, not that the weight-two residual p′-representation is unramified at p′.
For a normalized eigenform every theta iterate has first coefficient one. Thus repeated nonnegative theta powers are nonzero; do not assume an inverse theta operator exists.

imports.title: Auxiliary characteristic with prime-field coefficients
imports.statement: Let ρ̄ be an S-type representation in characteristic p, normalized to 2≤k(ρ̄)≤p+1 if p is odd. Assume cyclotomic absolute irreducibility if p is odd and nonsolvable image if p=2. Let C be the E-rational irreducible odd almost strictly compatible weight-two system supplied by KW I Theorem 5.1(2), with common ramification supported on S∪{p}, where S is the ramification of ρ̄ away from p. Either ρ̄ is modular, or for every bound B there is a prime p′>max(B,5,p,max S), with p′≡1 modulo 4 and splitting completely in E, and a place λ′|p′, such that C̄_λ′ is absolutely irreducible, defined over F_p′, of classical Serre weight two, with nonsolvable image and absolutely irreducible restriction to G_Q(μ_p′). Coefficient extensions and lattice reductions are understood up to common residue-field extension.
hypotheses: The common support S∪{p} is finite. Almost strict compatibility, rather than unconditional strict compatibility at every coefficient prime, suffices. Set max ∅=0 when S is empty.

Use the cofinite residual absolute-irreducibility conclusion of R24.6/residual-members for these fixed-weight bounded-conductor systems. A density-one conclusion alone cannot be intersected with an arbitrary splitting condition without further justification.
Complete splitting means residue degree one. Apply Chebotarev to the normal closure of E(i); no assumption that E/Q is Galois is made.
proofSteps: Exclude the finite exceptional set of residual reducibility and the common support. At an odd unramified coefficient prime p′>5, almost strict compatibility gives a crystalline member of weights {0,1}; the Fontaine–Laffaille comparison gives residual weight two.

Complete splitting gives residue degree one for the common Frobenius characteristic polynomials. Chebotarev on the finite residual image gives this property for every group element; apply the R15.6 finite-field semisimple realizability node to descend to F_p′. Splitting alone is not a chosen matrix model.

The ordinary inertia ratio has order p′−1; the niveau-two ratio has order p′+1. Thus the projective image contains an element of order at least six, excluding solvable exceptional projective groups A4 and S4. Dickson leaves the dihedral solvable case.
If restriction to Q(μ_p′) were reducible, the normalized bad-dihedral weight constraint would give weight (p′+1)/2 or (p′+3)/2, incompatible with two for p′>5.

Any dihedral candidate is already modular by the R17.5 solvable residual theorem. The odd-prime KW I Theorem 4.1 makes its crystalline weight-two lift modular. Equality of good Frobenius polynomials then makes C, and hence ρ̄, modular. This proves the first alternative without invoking the final Serre theorem.
Otherwise all eligible candidates are nonsolvable. Chebotarev supplies infinitely many completely split primes of the normal closure of E(i); remove the finite excluded primes and choose above B.
acceptance: The smallest prime satisfying p′>5 and p′≡1 modulo 4 is 13, with inertia-ratio orders 12 or 14. The candidate 7 tests only the order estimate, not the congruence condition.
A coefficient prime of residue degree greater than one is insufficient for the prime-field version of Lemma 8.2. Complete splitting must precede that application.
Trace and determinant congruences are transported through a common coefficient embedding and stable lattice, not an identification of unrelated residue fields.

imports.title: Exact weight and conductor from modularity
imports.statement: Let ρ̄ be modular and of S-type in characteristic p. Suppose p is odd, or p=2 and its classical Serre weight k(ρ̄) is two. Then there is a normalized primitive characteristic-zero cuspidal eigenform f of exact level N(ρ̄) and exact weight k(ρ̄), a coefficient place λ|p, a stable lattice and a residue-field embedding such that (ρ_f,λ mod λ)^ss≅ρ̄. The reduction of the nebentypus is the finite-order factor ε(ρ̄) of det ρ̄=ε(ρ̄)χ̄_p^(k(ρ̄)−1). The p=2 conclusion includes an actually scalar restriction to the full decomposition group at 2, irrespective of dihedrality. No claim of general Katz weight-one realization or exact Teichmüller nebentypus is made.
hypotheses: A modularity witness is an existing eigenform with the stated residual representation, of some weight and level; minimality of that witness is not assumed.

The actual scalar local restriction, rather than its semisimplification or a repeated Frobenius polynomial, is the scalar case. Its finite-image scalar character has odd order and is unramified at 2 by the imported local reciprocity lemma; finite étale implies finite flat and classical weight two.

Use the source notion of minimal lift, including its special characteristic-two induced case at odd primes. Conductor preservation is a property of those local conditions, not a consequence of retaining the same ramified-prime set.

Only the Lemma 6.2(i) dihedral exact-weight/level projection of the pre-existing R27.1 mixed-source node is used. Its supplier mathematics remains R17.5/R17.6, R20.5 and R15; no second dihedral theorem is planned here.

The final same-weight Katz-to-classical eigensystem comparison is the requested R15.2 input of gap G1. Deligne–Serre eigenvalue lifting applies only after a residual eigenvector in an integral reduction module is supplied. An arbitrary Katz form of weight at least two is not declared to lie in that image.
proofSteps: For dihedral projective image import the exact classical conclusion of KW I Lemma 6.2(i), with Wiese Theorem 1 and its classical Serre-weight consequence at p=2. The unramified branch first supplies Katz weight one at N, including scalar restrictions. Hasse multiplication gives weight two but does not itself prove integral liftability. The source classical conclusion is imported separately; the explicit geometric bridge is recorded in gap G1. The ramified branch uses dihedral automorphy and nonscalar optimization. Representations induced from Q(i) use the separate dihedral branch, never Buzzard Theorem 2.8.

For a nondihedral representation in odd characteristic, choose i with 2≤k(ρ̄⊗χ̄_p^i)≤p+1. The prime-to-p conductor stays N(ρ̄). Its cyclotomic restriction is absolutely irreducible. In characteristic two set i=0; nondihedral image is nonsolvable by the finite classification.

Type-(1) minimal crystalline lifting gives ρ_p of that normalized weight, minimal at all q≠p. Apply exactly KW I Theorem 4.1: the odd-prime crystalline branch, or its dyadic crystalline weight-two branch. The latter imposes no local nonscalar condition, so it covers the scalar nondihedral case.

Choose the primitive newform for this modular lift. Full local–global compatibility away from p gives its local conductor at q≠p equal to the lift’s minimal conductor. At p, the full coefficient-prime WD comparison identifies an unramified parameter with zero monodromy. R16.3/conductor-epsilon-comparison identifies its Artin exponent zero with the newvector exponent c(π_p); the R16.2 definition then supplies a GL₂(Z_p)-fixed vector and p∤level. Hodge weights fix the classical weight. Thus the level is exactly N, not just supported at the same primes.

For odd p, reduce the normalized newform and apply R15.3’s tame-level theta theorem a nonnegative number of times congruent to −i modulo p−1. Each iterate is nonzero because its first coefficient remains one. This preserves tame level and restores the original residual representation. Edixhoven supplies its classical Serre weight at N. Invoke the requested same-weight, same-tame-level eigensystem lifting comparison of gap G1; only then apply the integral/Deligne–Serre interface, allowing a compatible integral character and coefficient extension. A primitive associate has level M|N, while conductor comparison gives N|M, hence M=N. At p=2 there is no untwisting step.

For comparison with the earlier dyadic route: if the full local restriction is nonscalar, R20.5 supplies Buzzard multiplicity one and Theorem 3.2; for non-Q(i) induction its conductor descent uses Theorem 2.8 with residual unramifiedness at each removed odd prime. The scalar branch uses the minimal-lift argument above instead of supplying an unsupported multiplicity-one hypothesis.
acceptance: A nontrivial Jordan block with equal diagonal entries is nonscalar. It is admitted by the nonscalar multiplicity-one branch; a test based only on distinct eigenvalues is rejected.
A scalar dyadic representation with nonsolvable global image uses type-(1) lifting and dyadic Theorem 4.1 without any multiplicity-one premise.

At p=2 a dihedral unramified representation exceptional at 2 may have only a Katz weight-one witness at N. The conclusion is still classical weight two at N, with the weight-two lifting criterion made explicit.
Odd-p weights above p+1 require normalization and untwisting. A conclusion only for the normalized twist is insufficient.
In a Q(i)-induced example the proof never applies Buzzard Theorem 2.8, which excludes that family. Classical dyadic weight four is outside this theorem.

A Katz eigensystem in the requested weight must be supplied with the reduction-module comparison of G1 before Deligne–Serre is applied. A weight shift would prove only qualitative modularity and is insufficient for this exact-weight conclusion.

imports.title: Khare–Wintenberger Theorem 1.2
imports.statement: For any odd prime p, every S-type ρ̄ with odd prime-to-p conductor N(ρ̄) arises from a normalized characteristic-zero cuspidal newform of exact weight k(ρ̄) and exact level N(ρ̄). In characteristic two, every S-type ρ̄ with classical Serre weight two arises from such a newform of weight two and exact level N(ρ̄); its prime-to-two conductor is automatically odd. A coefficient place, stable lattice and residual coefficient embedding realize the residual isomorphism. The scalar dyadic local case is included.
hypotheses: Import HypD 0 from R27.3/d0-from-all-lr; do not reprove the double induction.

Odd-p even conductor and dyadic weight four are outside Theorem 1.2 and belong to R27.5. The theorem uses classical weights at least two; it does not assert the minimum-Katz-weight-one refinement for arbitrary scalar dyadic representations.
proofSteps: HypD 0 and the level-raising implication with r=0 give qualitative modularity in precisely the two stated ranges.
Apply strong-form-by-minimal-lifts to obtain the exact weight and level, including the dyadic scalar branch.
acceptance: The r=0 conductor predicate is oddness of N. In characteristic two it puts no new restriction on N, but the weight-two requirement remains essential.
A hypothetical input at p odd with v₂(N)=1, or at p=2 with k=4, cannot be passed to this theorem solely from HypD 0.
Do not replace the classical weight-two conclusion by Katz weight one in the scalar dyadic case.
